A student claimed that the lower DO concentrations at Station B at depths of 20 m and below were caused entirely by the water at Station B being warmer than the water at Station A, since warmer water holds less oxygen. Do Figures 1 and 2 support this claim?

options.A: No; at 25 m and 30 m the two stations had the same water temperature, yet the DO concentration at Station B was more than 3 mg/L lower.
options.B: No; a decrease in temperature with depth should have caused the DO concentration to increase with depth at both stations, and it did not.
options.C: Yes; the DO concentration at Station B was lower than the DO concentration at Station A at every depth from the surface to 30 m.
options.D: Yes; Station B was warmer than Station A at every depth at which both stations were measured, and warmer water holds less oxygen.
